title: Adopt buffered direct output for qualifying hosted partition shuffles
question: Can the hosted planner choose direct output cheaply and reliably for large partition shuffles while preserving the existing sort and publication contracts?
summary: Select a capped 512 KiB writer at the final traversal for qualifying hosted Partition then Uniform or Auto, at a validated output lower bound of 96 MiB and sufficient live headroom. A 3.253 GB spill job saved a paired median 9.764 s and reduced peak managed temporary storage from 6.781 GB to 3.529 GB.

workloads: Plain UTF-8 output, one worker, automatic grouping. Matched synthetic external and resident Runs, 32 MiB through 384 MiB fixed and applicable Auto memory tiers.
Held-out below and above the cutoff, 1,536 groups with a 64 KiB cap, a late wide record, and a 7.46 MB gzip input with 260.8 MB validated plain output.
Three 3.253 GB OPFS pairs with a 38-way merge. Three 563.1 MB desktop Chrome pairs with an actual ext4 destination and 22-way merge.

validation.summary: Every measured export verifies exact payloads, membership, names and caps. Observed routes, matched sort topology and memory tiers, marker ordering and cleanup passed. Fourteen injected or input failure cases, a late writer admission recipe with a held peer grant, and a 190 MiB managed quota control passed.

limitations: One WSL2 ext4 host with warm uncontrolled caches and synthetic layouts. Bundled Chromium used OPFS handles and desktop Chrome used actual picker grants in an isolated display.
The 96 MiB floor is a conservative selection boundary tested on this panel. Other workload crossovers can differ.
Spilling jobs retained nearly the same combined logical storage peak. The late shared-memory boundary models live owner overlap with controlled grants.
exclusions: Native throughput, RSS, CPU time, physical device traffic, compressed output, formulas, and other pipeline shapes.
Concurrent browser timing, other browser families, and other storage devices.
reopen_when: Additional output shapes qualify for a dedicated overlap and export assessment, or representative larger jobs show a different elapsed-time or admission boundary.
